sections.body: MEAN = total ÷ how many. MEDIAN = the middle value when sorted. MODE = the most common. RANGE = biggest − smallest.
One extreme value can pull the mean a lot, but barely moves the median.
Graphs can mislead: a y-axis that doesn't start at zero can make small differences look huge.
Probability ranges from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). A fair coin landing heads has probability ½.

hints: Find the middle one of five values.
For 1, 4, 6, 8, 9 the median is the 3rd value: 6.

quiz.q: A bar chart's y-axis starts at 95 instead of 0. Why might it mislead?
hints: What happens to the bars' heights?
A tiny difference fills more of the chart.
If two scores are 96 and 98 and the axis starts at 95, one bar looks three times the other.
quiz.explain: Starting above zero exaggerates small differences.
